title: HeroQuest - A Look at Some of the Newer (to me) Expansions
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=50FAA319hpc

Daniel (@dungeondive) tours four HeroQuest expansions acquired over the past year: Prophecy of Telor, Spirit Queen's Torment, The Crypt of Perpetual Darkness and Wizards of Morcar. He enjoys the new toys, but examines them through his preference for solo play and a flexible dungeon-crawling system rather than the standard one-versus-many format.

Prophecy of Telor and Spirit Queen's Torment bring quest books, translucent monsters and the Warlock and Bard heroes. Daniel sees a missed opportunity in those differently coloured monsters: separate cards with elite abilities would make them easier to shuffle into random encounters. He also wants more distinctive equipment and artifacts, with fewer rewards reduced to another potion or spell scroll.

The Crypt of Perpetual Darkness catches his attention with board overlays, a large dragon and unusually presented cards. Wizards of Morcar offers especially appealing spellcasting enemies, new hero spells, mercenaries and chunky monster sculpts. Its between-quest town visits are welcome, though he wishes the settlement phase offered more choices and random events. Missing reference cards for the enemy wizards prompt the same question about repurposing components outside their quest books.

Throughout, this is a look at what the boxes contain and how Daniel might fold them into his customised game. He closes by outlining future coverage of fan-made solo and co-op systems for players who want to take HeroQuest in similar directions.

----

What would you most like an official HeroQuest expansion to add: distinctive monsters, stranger artifacts, or a fuller travel and settlement phase?
